description:
SLIDING TACKLERS CAN NOW BE PUT ON THE GROUND. ONE INSTRUCTION, THREE BYTES. This is the one pack in this set that actually makes more bodies hit the deck, and it is the one to test first.

WHAT CHANGES. match::anime::action::Sliding::vf14 (0x143f70360) is the function that answers 'may a contact reaction interrupt the slide I am currently doing?'. Stock, it answers NO for the first part of every sliding tackle and only starts answering YES once the slide animation passes a key frame. This pack changes the refuse default from 0 to 1, so the answer is YES for the whole slide. A player who slides in and catches a body can now be staggered or put on the ground at any point in the slide instead of gliding through untouched. This is the classic missing picture: the slider goes through the man, clips him, and BOTH go down.

IT DOES NOT MAKE CONTACT HAPPEN MORE OFTEN. It removes a veto that is currently suppressing the reaction to contact the engine has already detected. Nothing about collision detection, contact scoring or the odds of a stagger changes.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE - your stick-controlled player, your AI team-mates and the CPU, identically. It is a property of the sliding action, and every player who slides runs the same code.

WHAT IS DEMONSTRATED (a-EMULATED). Sliding::vf14 was run under Unicorn on the INSTALLED image with its six anime-data callees stubbed (0x143e940a0 motion handle, 0x143e9a390 event count, 0x143e99b70 / 0x143e99e20 key frame, 0x143ea9040 current frame, 0x14533ea80 float helper). Over (currentFrame, keyFrame, eventCount) in {0,5,19,20,30} x {20} x {0,1,2}: STOCK returns 0 for cur<20 and 1 for cur>=20 in all 15 cases; WITH THIS PATCH it returns 1 in all 15. Independently re-verified this pass by full disassembly: r14b is written exactly once (0x143f7037d) and read exactly once (0x143f70428, 'movzx ecx,r14b' then 'cmovge ecx,1'), so the return is (currentFrame >= keyFrame) ? 1 : r14b and nothing else in the function touches that register. The routing is b-level but certain: Contact::vf2 (0x143f010b0, shared by Contact, Stagger, FallDown and Dive - confirmed from the vtables) sends current kinds 0x0b and 0x0c to currentAction->vf14, and the action registry built by 0x143eee750 was decoded this pass and puts BOTH 0x0b and 0x0c on the same Sliding object at pool+0x200.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN (c-INFERRED). What anime event type 5 actually is - it defines where the stock immunity window ends. That is why this is an all-or-nothing boolean and there is no gentler version: a graded variant would mean moving that key frame, which nobody has decoded.

KNOWN BREADTH, STATED HONESTLY. Sliding::vf14 never reads the incoming action's kind - verified by full disassembly this pass, the argument register is never touched. So the veto disappears for the WHOLE contact family, which is Stagger (0x10), FallDown (0x11), Dive (0x0f) and the plain Contact action, not only for falls. No case was found where that is wrong, but it has not been excluded either.

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS. No score term and no whistle or card threshold is touched - the foul model (scorer 0x143d88fe0, level function 0x143d861f0, lines at 40/60/80/110) is a completely separate system and this pack does not write into it. There IS an indirect effect and you should expect it: a slide that gets cut short before it reaches the ball loses the 'got the ball' excuse that the Judge's late-challenge window at 0x143d88658 tests. So expect a SMALL INCREASE IN FREE KICKS GIVEN AGAINST SLIDING TACKLES, and NO CHANGE AT ALL to the 80 and 110 card lines - yellows and reds should stay where they are.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN ONE MATCH. Watch sliding tackles specifically, both yours and the CPU's. You want: a tackler who catches the man as well as the ball going down himself, two bodies on the floor after a heavy slide, and slides that get stopped by a shoulder instead of sailing through. Count free kicks against slides - a small rise is expected and correct.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO STRONG. Slides dying instantly on the lightest brush - a tackler who crumples on frame 0 before he has travelled anywhere, which reads on screen as a player tripping over nothing. Also: slide tackles becoming useless because they are cancelled before they ever reach the ball. If you see either, pull this pack; it cannot be softened.

COLLISIONS: none. 0x143f7037d is byte-identical between the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE (both 4532F6, verified this pass). It is not in the already-applied kick-error code (0x14401b423, 0x14401a12c, 0x1440187b4, 0x14105ed1e) and does not overlap any unapplied spec - phys-tackle-commit (0x1441a7fa0/0x1441a8a70), phys-marking-tight, phys-duel-strength, duels-strength (0x14431145b), phys-jostle-push (0x143f56e39/0x143f56e64), phys-whistle-threshold, phys-late-challenge, phys-reckless-contact, cave-ability-error or linked-spin.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/falls-slide-tackle-contact.json

patches.name: a sliding tackler is no longer immune to contact reactions
patches.note: xor r14b,r14b -> mov r14b,1. Same length. r14b is the refuse default returned by Sliding::vf14 when the slide has not yet reached its key frame; written once here, read once at 0x143f70428 as 'movzx ecx,r14b' / 'cmovge ecx,edx(=1)'. Forcing it to 1 makes the function return 1 unconditionally. Site byte-identical in PRISTINE and the installed exe.
